statement: have x1 : (Fin (9 : ℕ) → Bool) → Bool := fun (x1 : Fin (9 : ℕ) → Bool) => x1 (0 : Fin (9 : ℕ)) && x1 (1 : Fin (9 : ℕ)) || x1 (1 : Fin (9 : ℕ)) && x1 (2 : Fin (9 : ℕ)) || x1 (2 : Fin (9 : ℕ)) && x1 (3 : Fin (9 : ℕ)) || x1 (3 : Fin (9 : ℕ)) && x1 (4 : Fin (9 : ℕ)) || x1 (4 : Fin (9 : ℕ)) && x1 (0 : Fin (9 : ℕ)) || x1 (0 : Fin (9 : ℕ)) && x1 (5 : Fin (9 : ℕ)) || x1 (1 : Fin (9 : ℕ)) && x1 (6 : Fin (9 : ℕ)) || x1 (2 : Fin (9 : ℕ)) && x1 (7 : Fin (9 : ℕ)) || x1 (3 : Fin (9 : ℕ)) && x1 (8 : Fin (9 : ℕ)) || x1 (5 : Fin (9 : ℕ)) && x1 (7 : Fin (9 : ℕ)) || x1 (6 : Fin (9 : ℕ)) && x1 (8 : Fin (9 : ℕ)) || x1 (8 : Fin (9 : ℕ)) && x1 (5 : Fin (9 : ℕ)); ∀ (x2 : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit),   have x3 : List PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Gate := List.map (fun (x3 : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Gate) => { op := x3.op, inputs := if x3.op.eval [Bool.false] = Bool.true then List.take (1 : ℕ) x3.inputs else x3.inputs : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Gate }) (List.drop (1 : ℕ) x2.gates);   have x4 : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Gate → Bool := fun (x4 : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Gate) => [(0 : ℕ), (9 : ℕ)].any fun (x5 : ℕ) => x4.inputs.contains x5;   have x5 : ℕ := (List.filter x4 x3).length;   PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.FanInTwo x2 → (∀ (x7 : Fin (9 : ℕ) → Bool), (x2.wires (List.ofFn x7)).getD (9 : ℕ) Bool.false = !x7 (0 : Fin (9 : ℕ))) → PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.circuitFun (9 : ℕ) x2 = x1 → x2.size ≤ (15 : ℕ) → x5 ≤ (1 : ℕ) → False

sketch: Step 3 of 4 of a checked cut of L-meta-1665. Its sibling steps: L-meta-2305, L-meta-2307, L-meta-2311. Together they give the parent; the parent's own sketch: a proof by cases is possible: one sibling case of this family (another first gate) was proved outright by exhaustive case analysis inside the checker's limits, as one long proof file. Same shape here: fix the first gate as stated, split on the next gates up to the symmetries that fix it, and close each branch by evaluation. title: Implicant lift: in a fan-in-two AND/OR circuit, an OR gate's input t that implies the output can be moved to a new top OR without changing the function
statement: ∀ (n : ℕ) (C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit) (j u t : ℕ), PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.Monotone2 C → j < C.gates.length → C.gates[j]? = some { op := PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.GateOp.or, inputs := [u, t] } → t < n + j → (∀ x : Fin n → Bool, (C.wires (List.ofFn x)).getD t false = true → PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.circuitFun n C x = true) → PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.circuitFun n { gates := C.gates.set j { op := PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.GateOp.or, inputs := [u] } ++ [{ op := PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.GateOp.or, inputs := [C.output, t] }], output := n + C.gates.length } = PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.circuitFun n C
unlocks: The tool the one-output line now imports: a move that brings a circuit to an OR of blocks at no cost in gates.
context: SKETCH: The circuit's value is monotone in the value of gate j. Where t is false, gate j equals u, so replacing the gate by u changes nothing. Where t is true the output is true by hypothesis, and the appended OR with t makes the new output true. Where t is false the appended OR returns the old output, which is unchanged. In Lean: an evaluation lemma for a circuit with one gate replaced (induction over the gate list), monotonicity of AND/OR evaluation in one wire, then the two cases. Size: about 90 minutes. No sorry, no new axiom. Own namespace for every declaration.
